claims.subject: alara
claims.source_excerpt: five shards of Alara were separate worlds for centuries
claims.summary: Alara had five long-separated shards: Bant, Esper, Grixis, Jund, and Naya.
claims.limitation: This profile does not supply the calendar date when the original division occurred. These are regions/shards, not five independent present-day planes.

claims.subject: alara
claims.summary: Each of Alara's five separated shards had access to three mana colors during its isolation.
claims.limitation: The profile states the three-color condition generally; the separate identity of each shard's three colors requires its own card/color evidence.

claims.subject: alara
claims.source_excerpt: all five colors of mana once more
claims.summary: Following the convergence, the rejoined Alara again flowed with all five mana colors.
claims.limitation: The profile supplies no Dominarian AR year for the convergence.

claims.subject: alara
claims.summary: As shard boundaries dissolved, formerly isolated cultures clashed and wars broke out across reunited Alara.
claims.limitation: The wars and convergence overlap in this prose; do not convert their descriptions into a precise BEFORE ordering in the master timeline.

claims.subject: esper_forces
claims.summary: Esper's forces attacked other Alaran shards while seeking carmot.
claims.limitation: The plane primer does not identify commanders or the outcomes of individual Esper invasions.

claims.subject: grixis_undead
claims.summary: Grixis undead attacked other Alaran shards with the aim of maiming, enslaving, and draining their inhabitants' life energy.
claims.limitation: This establishes the general invasion motive, not a named battle or a fate for any named individual.

claims.subject: jund_warriors
claims.source_excerpt: their "life hunts" to the newfound game
claims.summary: Jund's warriors expanded their life hunts to new prey and territories across reunited Alara.
claims.limitation: The source does not name the participants of a particular hunt or identify the exact destinations.

claims.subject: naya_armies
claims.summary: Naya's armies followed elven decrees and departed the jungle seeking answers to the Anima's visions.
claims.limitation: The profile does not explain whether those prophetic visions proved accurate or when their prophecies were fulfilled.

claims.subject: bant_armies
claims.source_excerpt: in the name of their guardian angels
claims.summary: Bant's armies defended their territory against horrors crossing former shard borders in the name of their guardian angels.
claims.limitation: This does not establish which specific angels commanded particular fights.

claims.subject: carmot
claims.source_excerpt: necessary to create more of their dwindling etherium
claims.summary: The Alara plane primer identifies carmot as necessary to make more etherium for Esper.
claims.limitation: The page does not explain the exact material or magical synthesis recipe.

remaining: Research the five shards' distinct civilizations and historical chronology using additional official primary sources; a single plane primer is not exhaustive.
Do not infer specific in-world years or a strict BEFORE relation from simultaneous conflict prose.
Do not treat the descriptive grouping of armies or undead as a formal canonical organization or confirm identities of unnamed participants.
Preserve the existing UP001 Bolas manipulation claim without duplicating or overriding it; the owner has not approved this pack.
